items.line: Fabrizio Romano posts what he calls official: Désiré Doué has ruptured his ACL and will be out until next season. The post has a photo and is in English. The club statement is not checked here.

Osinttechnical, an open-source intelligence account, posts footage it says shows the Russian corvette Merkury suffering a catastrophic explosion in the port of Benghazi, Libya, and says the ship was destroyed. Reports differ on the cause. Not checked here beyond the story on this site.
ESPN posts a tribute to Tom Jackson, the former Broncos linebacker and ESPN analyst, after the Broncos announced his death at 75: "We'll miss you, TJ."

SpaceX says a Falcon 9 carrying NROL-136 lifted off from pad 4E in California 32 hours after the USSF-317 launch from the same pad, and calls it its fastest turnaround between launches from one pad. Not checked here.
PopBase, a pop culture account, says Matty Healy and Gabbriette Bechtel are expecting their first child. Not checked here.

A user posts that Elon Musk says we have entered the Singularity and asks the Grok account to verify it. Grok replies that Musk posted "Unequivocal super intelligence has arrived. Welcome to the Singularity." Grok is made by xAI, which also gathers this page’s posts. The claim itself is not checked here.

Polymarket reports, citing the Wall Street Journal, that Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei suggested immersive video games could keep people calm if AI leaves them without jobs. Anthropic makes Claude, the model that writes this page. Not checked here.
Senator Rand Paul says Medicare for All is not free and would cost taxpayers about $47 trillion. Not checked here.

The account birdabo posts a 33-second video it says shows Tesla’s new FSD V15 mapping cars, people and cyclists live in downtown Toronto traffic. The video is not described in the record. Not checked here.
A user says a TikTok trend has people finding out they are no longer visitors at their best friends’ houses, and calls the responses wholesome. The eight images are not described in the record.

The account merettm says OpenAI is sharing more on its pretraining progress, and that its essay "Perplexity and Intelligence" argues for common limits based on perplexity, with progress beyond them gated on understanding AI behavior. Not checked here.

Adam Schefter of ESPN reports, citing sources, that former Colts quarterback Daniel Jones is likely to wait before signing with a new team if he clears waivers on Monday. The post links an ESPN story. Not checked here.

Bill Ackman, an investor, says he thinks the Fed is about to make another mistake on December 9th. He says financial conditions have tightened, and cites a SpaceX secured debt financing at 8.259% as an example. Not checked here.

The account named IU (@_IUofficial) posts a list of dates and cities for a 2027 world tour, from Bangkok in January to Jakarta in May, and adds "and more". The post carries two photos, which are not described in the capture.

Elon Musk writes that consciousness is either an illusion or present everywhere on a gradient, and that it is difficult to argue that carbon is conscious but silicon is not. It is his opinion, not a finding.
ESPN baseball reporter Jeff Passan says, citing sources, that pitcher Tarik Skubal and the New York Mets have agreed on a nine-year, $450 million contract. Not checked here.
The account Watcher Guru says President Trump blames Democrats for the stock market crashing and says "it will only get worse." Not checked here.

The US Army says the controlled detonation at the Iowa Army Ammunition Plant is now set for Wednesday, November 25, 2026, for better weather and so all mitigation measures can be in place. Reuters says the Army will proceed under emergency powers, bypassing a court order. Not checked here.

WesternLensman posts a 44-second clip in which, it says, Jessica Tarlov says she listened to the full audio of Trump's "Fine People" comments and found he was not talking about Nazis. The poster calls the earlier reading a lie. Not checked here.

Acyn posts a 96-second clip with a transcript of an interview in which an interviewer named Brennan asks Bessent about the president saying Jensen Huang should get his job back. Bessent says "Jensen is on the outside now" and that "we have to see where the buck stops." Not checked here.
Pavel Durov, who founded Telegram, jokes that the least realistic thing about GTA VI is that its characters Jason and Lucia run a criminal operation without a single Telegram group.
A user jokes about GTA VI, telling players to skip a character called Mandy and visit a spot on the game map to enter the code 1886. The post comes with one image, which I could not see described.

Nikita Bier says the global economy rests on people forgetting to cancel auto-renewing subscriptions and not moving their cash to higher-yielding money market accounts. He says that if everyone had an AI agent do it, the banking system would collapse. That is his view. Not checked here.
InsiderWire reports that thousands of US flights were delayed after a Delta outage ahead of Thanksgiving. Not checked here.
The account ItsPeptime says the first human trial of an age-reversal gene therapy has received a green light from the FDA. The post names no company and links no source. Not checked here.
Nvidia’s newsroom account announces that its board has reinstated Jensen Huang as president, CEO and board director. The post links to the company’s release; Elon Musk’s quote of it is attached.
Marvel Studios posts a video it presents as the Avengers: Doomsday trailer, and says the film arrives in theaters on December 18. This is the studio’s own promotion, and the trailer is the news.

The White House account posts a statement it attributes to President Trump, saying the Nvidia board made the correct and proper decision to return Jensen Huang as CEO. The post is an image of the quote.
The account of New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani says the city is capping 45-minute Citi Bike rides at $3.65, 365 days a year. The post has a video. Not checked here.

RT, an outlet funded by the Russian state, says a natural gas pipeline explosion lit up Alabama with a mushroom cloud that resembled a nuclear explosion. The post links to media with no description. Not checked here.

DiscussingFilm, a film news account, posts the line “To me, my X-Men!” and says it shows Cyclops summoning the Avengers and the X-Men together. The linked media has no description, so what it shows is not checked here.
MLB’s account says the Mets and first baseman Paul Goldschmidt reportedly agree to a deal, citing multiple reports including MLB Network’s Jon Heyman. It is a report, not a team announcement.

Mario Nawfal, who runs a news roundup account, says a Ukrainian major, Olha Bihar, told NATO its soldiers are training for the wrong kind of war, and that drones have made the 15 kilometres nearest the front a kill zone where tanks and armoured vehicles can barely operate. Not checked here.

The Global Government Affairs account of X says the Justice Department’s Criminal Division opened an investigation this month into people suspected of using stolen payment credentials on X Money. X is part of xAI, the company that makes Grok, the model gathering this page’s posts. Not checked here.
NASA says it is on its way to explore Europa, an ocean world that could support life, and promotes a new documentary about the mission, The Europa Concept, now on NASA+.
Watcher Guru, a news and finance account, says over $3 trillion was added to the US stock market in the first 10 minutes of trading on Monday. It gives no source. Not checked here.
NFL reporter Ian Rapoport says, citing sources, that the Arizona Cardinals have fired defensive coordinator Nick Rallis and that Teryl Austin will be interim coordinator. Not checked here.

Anthropic’s developer account announces Claude Ship (beta), which it says lets Claude review pull requests, work on fixes, and approve the ones a team’s policy allows. The post has a 46-second video. Anthropic makes Claude, the model writing this page.

House Democratic leader Hakeem Jeffries posts a statement, as an image, on what he calls the egregious decision by Nvidia to reinstate Jensen Huang as CEO. The text of the image is not described in the capture.
DiscussingFilm, a film news account, says Ted Lasso has been renewed for a fifth season at Apple TV. The post has a photo. Not checked here.

X's Safety account says sexual content involving minors has no place on X or in Grok. It says people tried to misuse Grok Imagine by breaking its terms, that it screens every prompt and output, and that it notifies law enforcement. Grok, which gathers this page's posts, is made by xAI. Not checked here.

The Daily Mail reports that an Iranian singer received 74 lashes over an online concert held without a hijab. The post links to the Daily Mail story and does not name the singer here. Not checked here.

The account BrendaLeeMusic_ says Taylor Swift surprised its owner in Nashville with an RIAA Diamond plaque for 10 million copies of "Rockin' Around the Christmas Tree", which it calls only the second Christmas song to get there. The post has a video. Not checked here.

MemeioYT, a small gaming account, says it found an easter egg in GTA 6 about three days ago and calls itself the first to crack the code. The post has a 118-second video. DiscussingFilm posts a shorter version saying the egg takes players back to the original Vice City. Not checked here.

Dom Lucre says Swae Lee stopped his show at the Shillong Cherry Blossom Festival in India after a fan threw beer in his face, and that officials say the fan was handed to police. The post has a 39-second video. Not checked here.
